en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Twenty-second Chapter
The Discourse on Imperturbability:
Is it the case that an arahant, established in imperturbability, attains final nibbāna?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that an Arahant, remaining in his natural state of consciousness, attains Parinibbāna? Yes.
If an Arahant, remaining in his natural state of consciousness, attains Parinibbāna, then indeed, you must not say:
“The Arahat, established in the imperturbable, attains final Nibbāna.
Is it true that the Arahat, established in the imperturbable, attains final Nibbāna?
Yes, it is.
“Does an Arahant attain final Nibbāna while established in a functional consciousness?
One should not say so... [etc. ...
“Does an Arahant not rather attain final Nibbāna while established in a resultant consciousness?”
“Yes.

[The opponent asks: “If an Arahant, while established in a resultant consciousness, attains final Nibbāna, then surely it should not be said that ‘an Arahant attains final Nibbāna while established in the imperturbable’?”
Is it the case that an arahant, established in the imperturbable, attains final nibbāna? Yes.
Is it the case that an arahant, established in a functional-ineffective state of consciousness, attains final nibbāna?
It should not be said thus...
[as before] ...Is it not the case that an Arahant, established in a resultant indeterminate state of consciousness, attains Parinibbāna?
Yes, it is.

If an arahant, while established in a resultant indeterminate state of consciousness, attains final nibbāna, then indeed it should not be said that "an arahant attains final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable.
Is it the case that an arahant attains final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable?
“Yes.
“But did the Blessed One pass away immediately after emerging from the fourth jhāna?
“Yes.”
If the Blessed One, having emerged from the fourth jhāna, attained final nibbāna immediately thereafter, then indeed it should not be said:
"An arahant attains final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable.
The Discussion on the Imperturbable is finished.
